name: SOA
label: Dischord
lede: Ten songs on a seven-inch, paid for out of a Georgetown ice cream manager's wages, by a band that was finished before its first birthday.

eras.title: The roadie takes the mic
eras.text: Henry Garfield spent 1980 hauling gear for The Teen Idles and scooping ice cream in Georgetown. When Minor Threat poached the Extorts' frontman, the three players left behind went looking for a singer, and found the scene's most intense fan.

years.h: The Teen Idles' roadie gets a turn
years.p: Garfield is carrying amps for [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] when singer Nathan Strejcek misses a practice. Garfield talks the band into letting him sing. It's a rehearsal, not a gig, but it plants the idea.

q: We're too scared to approach him.
years.h: The Extorts lose a singer and find one behind an ice cream counter
years.p: [[Lyle Preslar|c1b9b78e-691f-424d-8ce1-53c87c24d299]] leaves the Extorts to play guitar with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] in what becomes [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]. [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]], Wendel Blow and Simon Jacobsen recruit Garfield, and SOA is born.
years.xp:
The three Extorts knew exactly who they wanted and were too intimidated to ask him. They sent [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] as go-between, and the meeting happened at the Häagen-Dazs in Georgetown where Garfield was working as a manager. Hampton remembered him as the Teen Idles' roadie guy.

After that it was practice every other day: parents' basements, Dischord House, even rooms in Kalorama mansions. Garfield, Hampton said later, always charmed the moms.

years.h: First show: the D.C. scene gets a harder edge
years.p: SOA play out for the first time in December. Dischord's own history says the band brought a new level of aggression to the music, and that it matched the mood of the scene's younger kids exactly.

years.h: On the bill at the Unheard Music Festival
years.p: Two nights at d.c. space, the downtown arts space, in the band's first month on stage.

years.h: Eight songs with Skip Groff at Inner Ear
years.p: The band's first session ever, with Skip Groff producing at Inner Ear Studio in Arlington. Two of these takes will end up on Flex Your Head, one on the EP, and the rest will sit in the vault for 33 years.

eras.title: Ice cream money and a one-way ticket
eras.text: SOA lasted about as long as a school year. In that time they made Dischord's second record, paid for by their singer, and played their final show on the same night that singer stepped into the band that would take him to California.

years.p: SOA play the 9:30 Club on F Street, one of the handful of shows the band ever played.

years.src: Dischord Records · Wikipedia · WJLA oral history
years.p: Ten songs on a seven-inch, recorded at Inner Ear with Skip Groff. Garfield was so eager to get it out that he paid for the recording and the pressing himself. Tina Angelos shot the cover photo; Hampton and Chris Edwards designed the sleeve.
years.xp:
Dischord was only one record old, with [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]]' Minor Disturbance as No. 1. The label had no money for a second release, and Garfield had a steady paycheck from Häagen-Dazs. [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] later put it simply: the ice cream job funded Dischord's second record.

The session work ran from December 1980 into January 1981. The EP went out of print on vinyl long ago, but the songs have never been hard to find: Dischord has kept them in circulation on compilations ever since.

years.h: A new drummer, and practice at the Naval Observatory
years.p: [[Ivor Hanson|a17981f7-ab3d-46dc-859a-582ac894cb20]] takes over from Simon Jacobsen. Hanson's father is a U.S. Navy admiral, so the band rehearses at the Naval Observatory. By Hanson's own count, he plays exactly one show with SOA

q: Henry's last show with SOA was his first show with Black Flag.
years.src: Dischord Records · WJLA oral history · Wikipedia
years.p: SOA open for Black Flag in Philadelphia. Garfield also sings with the headliners, and the night ends in a riot. The band breaks up that month.
years.xp:
Dischord's history records the riot plainly. The oral history puts it down to tensions with the neighborhood around the venue, not to anything that happened on stage. It was one of only a handful of SOA shows: the WJLA oral history counts about five, Wikipedia about a dozen.

For Hanson, the show was a hinge: Garfield sang SOA songs to open and then sang with Black Flag. It was the end of one band and the start of his next.

years.cap: Garfield's first official Black Flag show, Cuckoo's Nest, Costa Mesa.
years.p: A fan since getting the Nervous Breakdown EP, he had sung Clocked In with [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] at a New York bar show when Dez Cadena let him up, then passed an audition at Tu Casa Studio. He quits Häagen-Dazs, takes the surname Rollins, a name he and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] had used as teenagers, and plays his first official Black Flag show at the Cuckoo's Nest in Costa Mesa, California.

years.h: Hampton and Hanson go straight into [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]]
years.p: With Garfield gone west, [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] and [[Ivor Hanson|a17981f7-ab3d-46dc-859a-582ac894cb20]] start a new band with [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]] and Chris Bald. The Hampton and Hanson partnership will run on through Faith and [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]].

eras.title: The records outlive the band
eras.text: SOA were gone before most of D.C. had heard them on vinyl. Dischord kept the songs moving anyway, first on the sampler that defined the early scene and then on a 12-inch that gathered the label's first singles.

years.h: Three more songs on Flex Your Head
years.p: I Hate the Kids, Disease and Stepping Stone Party land on Dischord's compilation of the early D.C. bands, next to [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and [[Void|960a1d2f-2b5f-4fcf-bf11-4957529a6508]].
Dischord reissues the EP on Four Old 7"s on a 12", gathering its earliest singles onto one LP.

eras.title: The vault opens
eras.text: Once Dischord started mining its own history, SOA came back into print again and again. The last surprise was the band's very first recording session, released more than three decades after it happened.

years.h: On CD for the first time
years.p: No Policy joins the other 1981 singles on Dischord 1981: The Year in Seven Inches.
Dischord picks the song for 20 Years of Dischord, its anniversary box of the label's bands.

The Skip Groff session from December 1980, released on colored vinyl. Of the eight songs, five had never been heard in these versions. More than 33 years after the tape rolled, the first SOA recording became the last SOA release.
